unanswered_parts: Which exact part has failed when the general warning symbol is on

claims.text: The manual describes the warning symbol in the tell-tales as an indicator that glows whenever a vehicle component faults.

The manual lists the engine MIL separately: it stays continuously ON in case of an EMS malfunction, and the ABS lamp separately lights up for an ABS system malfunction. These are different indicators from the general warning symbol.

This partly answers your question. The retrieved manual information does not establish which exact part has failed when the general warning symbol is on; the symbol only indicates that some vehicle component has a fault.

Do not run the motorcycle if the malfunction indication remains ON continuously, as it can cause severe damage to the ECU and sensors; visit the nearest authorised Royal Enfield dealer to diagnose and rectify the EMS defect.

The ABS indicator is ON during the initial check-up (until or after the vehicle has run a particular distance/speed) and turns OFF if the system is OK; it lights up again in case of any ABS system malfunction. Do not run the motorcycle if the ABS indicator lamp remains continuously ON.
